**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 11 ("Transition Assistance and Data Return") already delivers our preferred position in full:

- **§11.1** — up to six months' transition assistance on expiry or termination for any reason, at our request, priced at the rates in the expiring Order Form (better than "then-current rates"), and expressly covering knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at existing scope/service levels.
- **§11.2** — return of all Customer Data within 30 days in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format with relationships and metadata, plus an express bar on withholding data over a fee dispute.
- **§11.3** — secure deletion only *after* we confirm successful return, written certification by an authorized officer, and continued protection of any copy retained under Applicable Law.

Cross-references check out: §10.1 preserves access through the agreed transition period and our Customer Data rights, §10.2 handles Deliverables and prepaid-fee refunds, and §16.5 expressly subordinates Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15 so the general "return or destroy" confidentiality duty cannot force premature deletion. Nothing here approaches the walk-away scenario.
